newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung seeks Dfl 565 mln to save Fokker -- radio.
newsitem.headline: Samsung seeks Dfl 565 mln to save Fokker -- radio.

text.p: Samsung Aerospace is seeking 565 million guilders ($329 million) in subsidies from the Dutch government to save bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker, a Dutch radio station said on Saturday.
Samsung has called for 165 million guilders in restart costs and 400 million for the development of a new 125-seater aircraft, Rijnmond Radio said.

The radio station also quoted Wim van Gelder, aviation spokesman for Labour, the dominant partner in the ruling coalition, as saying that Samsung's request for 565 million guilders should cause no problems.
No-one was available for comment either from the government or Fokker's receivers on Saturday.
On Thursday, the Dutch government said it was optimistic that talks between Samsung and Fokker would start in the coming week.

Earlier in the week, Samsung delivered a business plan for Fokker to the Dutch government. The South Korean planemaker wants the Dutch government to take a minority stake in a new Fokker and provide large subsidies.
Fokker was declared bankrupt in March, two months after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace said it was no longer willing to bear the company's huge losses.
The firm has since been kept alive artificially by court-appointed receivers.
